name: Lake Tschida - Crappie Creek Campground (Grant County)
note: Lake Tschida camping area on both sides of the Crappie Creek cove on the north shore, with a boat ramp, fish cleaning and a boat wash at its comfort station. The electric sites are long gravel pads in a loop set back behind a tree belt and marsh; the primitive sites are mown grass with a table and fire ring and no posted size, and 3-10, 13-18, 25-26 and 33-36 of them sit at the water. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: laketschida.org/crappie-creek (BOR/JJDA per-site map) + booking pages crappie-creek-electric (sites 40-54) and crappie-creek-primitive-1/-2 (3-26, 33-39), Peek program 'CRAPPIE CREEK ELECTRICAL CAMPSITES' selling single nights; operator photos show long gravel pads on the electric loop -> real drive-in RV campground. Separate from 6025 Rimrock (~4.7 km, across the lake, own access road). Operator Lake Tschida Recreation (Tri-Cities Joint Job Development Authority, the managing partner with the Bureau of Reclamation; same operator and ownership as 6025 Rimrock), laketschida.org read 2026-11-12. 'Camping unit' covers motor homes and pull-type campers (campground rules). Horse rule passes: the Hidden Shelter page says it is 'the only campground at Lake Tschida that will accommodate horses' and it is a separate area. Long-stay test 4: every site is sold by the night on Peek; the private cabin and trailer permittee areas are separate lease areas, not campground sites. Public (local): no price gate or presence rule.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: official BOR/JJDA Crappie Creek per-site map and the operator's Peek site photos put primitive 3-10, 13-18, 25-26 and 33-36 on open mown grass at the water's edge; Esri World Imagery (frames at 46.6185,-101.8616, the east arm ~46.6160,-101.8583 and the south loop) agrees: the south loop 33-36 is ~15-20 m from the shore across open grass, no treeline. Electric 40-54 sit behind a tree belt and marsh off the cove: no water value. Heart Butte Dam is ~4 km E; no dam check needed.
fees_source: https://laketschida.org/camping-fees ('$14 nightly fee for a primitive campsite at all campsites'; '$24 nightly fee for electrical campsites.'), read 2026-11-12

sites.note: Electric 40-54 on gravel pads; primitive 3-26 and 33-39 on grass (11 and 37 ADA).

booking.note: Online booking closes 7 days out; inside a week, book by phone with the office. Friday or Saturday arrivals must take two nights between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Unreserved sites are first come, first served with envelopes at the self-registration kiosks (cash or check).

flags: Electric amperage is not published (booking page, map and Peek tickets are silent), so hookups is left out rather than guessed.
Primitive sites are grass with no posted size; kept under the unclear-pad rule (an RV 'camping unit' is allowed at every site).
Crappie-creek-primitive-1 says a public path to the water now runs alongside site 14.
No season is published for any Lake Tschida area.
